Censor simulated event histories

Source: R/censoring.R
add_censoring.Rd

The simulation itself censors administratively at the end of the time grid. add_censoring() adds censoring that happens earlier: it cuts every trajectory at its censoring time, shortens the episode that contains it and drops everything after it.

Usage

add_censoring(data, times = NULL, rate = 0.1, keep_censoring_time = FALSE)

Arguments

data

Simulated event histories, as returned by sim_pexp(), sim_pexp_cr() or sim_pexp_msm().

times

Either a numeric vector of censoring times, named by id or in the order of the subjects, or a function of the number of subjects returning such a vector. Defaults to exponential censoring times, see rate.

rate

Rate of the exponential censoring distribution, used when times is not given.

keep_censoring_time

Append the censoring time of each subject as the column censoring_time.

Value

data with trajectories cut at the censoring times. Episodes that contain the censoring time get status = 0, to = NA and tstop equal to the censoring time; later episodes are removed. Subjects censored before their first episode begins drop out entirely.

Details

Censoring that depends on covariates or on the state of the process does not need this function: give the process a transition into a censoring state and name that state in censoring_states of sim_pexp_msm(). The engine then draws the censoring time from its own hazard, in competition with the other transitions, which is the natural way to express dependent censoring – dependent in the sense of covariates, not of the unobserved future.

Examples

df  <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100))
sim <- sim_pexp(~ log(0.2) + 0.3 * x, df, cut = seq(0, 10, by = 0.1))
add_censoring(sim, rate = 0.1) |> head()
#>   id episode from   to tstart     tstop status transition            x
#> 1  1       1    0    1      0 8.2974118      1       0->1 -1.400043517
#> 2  2       1    0    1      0 0.1030237      1       0->1  0.255317055
#> 3  3       1    0 <NA>      0 1.0312832      0       <NA> -2.437263611
#> 4  4       1    0    1      0 0.7301007      1       0->1 -0.005571287
#> 5  5       1    0 <NA>      0 0.3253287      0       <NA>  0.621552721
#> 6  6       1    0    1      0 0.6014634      1       0->1  1.148411606

# fixed end of follow-up per subject, e.g. staggered study entry
add_censoring(sim, times = runif(100, 2, 10)) |> head()
#>   id episode from   to tstart     tstop status transition            x
#> 1  1       1    0 <NA>      0 7.9441459      0       <NA> -1.400043517
#> 2  2       1    0    1      0 0.1030237      1       0->1  0.255317055
#> 3  3       1    0 <NA>      0 5.9746020      0       <NA> -2.437263611
#> 4  4       1    0    1      0 0.7301007      1       0->1 -0.005571287
#> 5  5       1    0 <NA>      0 9.6633530      0       <NA>  0.621552721
#> 6  6       1    0    1      0 0.6014634      1       0->1  1.148411606
